content.text:
The answer is yes, within each type. Aligned on its release date, every interim release has about 6 months of development and 9 months of support (18 months up to 12.10). Every LTS release since 14.04 has 5 years of standard support, ESM until year 10, and Legacy until year 15. The early LTS releases (6.06–10.04, plus 12.04) had shorter cycles with extended server support.

The deliverable is `/work/spec.vl.json`. `render` finished with status OK and no warnings.

```
REPORT
deliverable: spec.vl.json
requirements:
  R1: done - one row per release, labelled by version, sorted by release date within each group
  R2: done - x = years since own release (0 = release), unit in axis title
  R3: done - five phases as coloured bars with legend; missing or zero-length phases are not drawn
  R4: done - black circle = created, black diamond = release on every row
  R5: done - two stacked panels (LTS / Interim) sharing one x scale
  R6: done - title plus a one-sentence caption (subtitle) stating the pattern
assumptions:
  - Release type is LTS when the version contains "LTS"
  - Years = days / 365.25
  - Extended server phase only when eol-server > eol; ESM starts at the later of eol and eol-server
  - Missing trailing CSV fields are treated as "no date"
limitations:
  - Planned (future) dates are drawn the same as past dates; nothing marks today
  - Caption numbers are written by hand from what the figure shows; the figure itself is computed from the data
  - The subtitle line is long and reaches close to the right edge at 1400 px
```
